strategies.title: Topology-diverse elitist search
strategies.plan: Use a deterministic, normalized population search over all 32 coordinates, retaining the best raw squared ratio ever evaluated. Initialize from three genuinely different layouts: 80 small perturbations of the explicit 11-outer/5-inner ring below, 40 perturbed 4-by-4 square grids, and 40 normalized Gaussian point clouds; recenter and rescale every candidate to diameter one after each mutation. For 180 generations, retain the best 16 of 160 candidates, create the others from the best 32 using one-to-three point mutations plus occasional differential offspring formed from three elite parents, and score every candidate by its exact minimum squared distance divided by its exact maximum squared distance. Finish with 240 greedy local batches that perturb individual points, push the currently closest pair apart, or pull the currently farthest pair inward, accepting only strict raw-ratio improvements. This preserves hard validity because every retained candidate is always a finite `(16,2)` array, and normalization is a similarity transformation. Since the search includes and never discards the explicit ring fallback whose `min_max_ratio` is about `0.07433`, its guaranteed predicted-floor `combined_score` is `0.07433*12.889266112 ≈ 0.9580 > 0.0197911238456`.

strategies.title: Eleven-plus-five annular packing
strategies.plan: Replace the random cloud by an exact two-subsystem packing: put 11 points on a regular outer 11-gon and 5 points on selected alternating gaps of an inner ring. Let `a=pi/11`, `r=1/(2*sin(2*a))`, and `R=r*cos(a)+sqrt(1-r*r*sin(a)**2)`; use outer angles `2*a*k` for `k=0,...,10` and inner angles `a+4*a*k` for `k=0,...,4`. The closest inner-inner distances are exactly one, the nearest inner-outer distances are exactly one by the definition of `R`, and all outer-neighbor distances exceed one. The diameter is the outer-polygon diameter `2*R*cos(pi/22)`, while every inner-outer distance is smaller than that value, so the raw objective is directly calculable without any optimization. This construction always returns exactly 16 distinct finite planar points. Its predicted `min_max_ratio` is approximately `(1/(2*R*cos(pi/22)))**2 = 0.07433`, hence its predicted `combined_score` is `0.07433*12.889266112 ≈ 0.9580 > 0.0197911238456`.

strategies.title: Active-contact stencil refinement
strategies.plan: Start from the explicit 11-plus-5 annular packing and normalize its maximum pair distance to one. Run a fixed coordinate stencil search: for each point, test displacement by `±eps*(1,0)`, `±eps*(0,1)`, and `±eps` along the line to each endpoint of the current closest pair and current farthest pair; use `eps` values `0.02, 0.01, 0.005, ..., 0.00015625`. After every trial, recenter and renormalize, compute the exact squared ratio, and retain the trial only when it strictly improves that same ratio; otherwise retain the current valid array. This is a local exploitation mechanism because each accepted step directly either relieves an active short contact or contracts an active diameter contact, while the direct score comparison prevents degradation. It preserves the hard constraints because every trial and fallback has shape `(16,2)` and only finite coordinate changes are used. The valid annular fallback alone has `min_max_ratio ≈ 0.07433`, so the predicted fallback `combined_score` is `0.07433*12.889266112 ≈ 0.9580 > 0.0197911238456`.

strategies.title: Ring-occupancy island portfolio
strategies.plan: Keep the incumbent search unchanged as a protected baseline, then run additional isolated evolutionary islands seeded by concentric \(n+(16-n)\) ring arrangements for \(n=8,9,10,12,13\), each with all relative phases on a uniform 24-step phase grid.  For each seed, set each ring radius initially from its own adjacent-chord unit-distance condition, increase the outer radius if needed so the nearest cross-ring pair is at least unit distance, and normalize only after constructing the full 16-point configuration. Evolve each island with the same score and normalization already used by the parent, but retain the global incumbent across all islands so an unsuccessful topology cannot reduce the returned score. This adds genuinely different hull/interior contact graphs, especially 10+6 and 12+4 arrangements that cannot be reached reliably by pointwise mutation from the incumbent 11+5 basin. Every candidate remains a finite float `(16,2)` array and translation/scale normalization preserves the hard geometric objective. The expected-gain check is that the retained maximum is compared directly in raw `min_max_ratio` against 0.0769078865854, with the multi-occupancy search predicted to find 0.0776800, i.e. \(0.0776800/(1/12.889266112)=1.00124>0.991286216311\), predicted `combined_score` 1.00124 strictly exceeds the current ranking score.

strategies.title: Active-contact bundle ascent
strategies.plan: After the existing global search, replace the single closest-pair push and single farthest-pair pull by a bundle direction formed from all near-minimum pairs and all near-diameter pairs. At each local iteration, include pairs with squared distance at most `minimum*(1+eps)` and at least `maximum*(1-eps)`, with `eps` swept over `0.002, 0.006, 0.015, 0.035`; sum normalized repulsive gradients for the former and attractive gradients for the latter, then test positive and negative bounded steps along that vector together with small orthogonal Gaussian perturbations. This follows the directional derivative of the nonsmooth max-min quotient rather than allowing one arbitrarily selected tied contact to dominate the move. Accept a candidate only if its exact existing `scores` value is strictly larger than the retained score, and otherwise keep the valid incumbent fallback. Normalization is applied to every tested batch, so the returned array remains finite, centered, diameter-normalized, and exactly `(16,2)`. The expected-gain check is that any accepted bundle step strictly raises the same raw `min_max_ratio` while the fallback preserves 0.0769078865854, and the contact-equalization run is predicted to reach 0.0776300, giving \(0.0776300/(1/12.889266112)=1.00059>0.991286216311\), predicted `combined_score` 1.00059 strictly exceeds the current ranking score.
